catalysts: Up-cycle continuation: stronger-than-modeled customer equipment and services spend in leading-edge logic, HBM, and advanced packaging.
Margin inflection: improved utilization/mix and operating leverage translating into higher EBIT margins than base case.

Order/backlog durability and execution against capacity expansions (supply chain, manufacturing throughput). ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/12/3237648/0/en/Applied-Materials-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results.html))
company_overview: Applied Materials provides semiconductor process equipment and related services/software across two reportable segments: Semiconductor Systems and Applied Global Services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000119312526027318/d54380dars.pdf))

Semiconductor Systems includes tools for materials engineering steps such as etch, deposition, rapid thermal processing, metrology/inspection, and related technologies. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000119312526027318/d54380dars.pdf))

Applied Global Services includes spares, upgrades, services, and factory automation software designed to optimize equipment and fab productivity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000119312526027318/d54380dars.pdf))
current_context: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $7.01 billion (down 2% y/y); GAAP operating margin was 26.1% and GAAP operating income was $1.83 billion. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/12/3237648/0/en/Applied-Materials-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results.html))

Company guided Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $7.65 billion +/- $0.50 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.64 +/- $0.20. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/12/3237648/0/en/Applied-Materials-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results.html))

Management commentary emphasized continued AI-driven acceleration in leading-edge logic, HBM/advanced packaging, and capacity planning. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/12/3237648/0/en/Applied-Materials-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results.html))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth assumes continued semiconductor capex support (AI compute and memory upgrades) with gradually moderating growth post-cycle peak.

EBIT margin is modeled to remain near the historical ~0.29 operating margin regime, reflecting operating leverage plus ongoing services/mix support. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000119312526027318/d54380dars.pdf))

D&A intensity is held broadly stable as a percent of sales, consistent with recent D&A history across FY2023-FY2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000119312526027318/d54380dars.pdf))

Capex is normalized to a sustainable level (relative to 2025) and working capital intensity is modeled to trend toward the lower end of the recent range. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000119312526027318/d54380dars.pdf))
key_risks: Semiconductor equipment cyclicality: revenue and margins can decline quickly if wafer-fab spending slows.
Geopolitical/trade restrictions (including China-related export controls) can reduce TAM and shift mix/visibility.
Working-capital and capex normalization risk: modeled assumptions may diverge from actual cash conversion and investment cycles.

presentation.subtitle: Applied Materials (AMAT) DCF input pack: AI cycle, margins, and working-capital discipline
valuation_summary: DCF uses a Gordon Growth terminal approach (no terminal exit multiple) with a conservative terminal growth rate and a WACC calibrated from market-data inputs.
Comparable-company reference points use semicap equipment/testing peer enterprise valuation multiples (EV/Sales, EV/EBITDA) and forward P/E as sanity checks against cycle-adjusted margins.
Scenario analysis applies modest deltas to growth, margins, WACC, and terminal growth rather than extreme valuation swings.
